sources.title: Thailand's National Adaptation Plan (NAP)
sources.organization: Office of Natural Resources and Environmental Policy and Planning, Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment, Thailand
sources.temporal_coverage: National adaptation plan; provincial climate-risk rankings modelled for 2016–2035 under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5.
sources.methodology: National plan reproduces ONEP consultant models and sectoral risk assessments for climate adaptation planning.
sources.limitations: Provincial top-ten lists are model outputs attributed to ONEP 2021, not measured current impacts; the settlements-and-security sector label is not a conflict indicator.

sources.title: Thailand Country Climate and Development Report
sources.temporal_coverage: Published 2025; includes historical/current diagnostics, projections and a Khon Kaen provincial water-management case.
sources.methodology: World Bank country assessment with biophysical modeling and policy analysis; Industrial Economics supported physical-risk modeling.
sources.limitations: Model scenarios and dates are stated claim-by-claim; the Khon Kaen institutional case describes planning processes, not evaluated climate-resilience outcomes.

sources.title: Climate Change Adaptation Implementation and Governance in Thailand: Increased Resilience and Potential Conflicts
sources.organization: Springer Nature, in Risks, Resilience and Interdependency
sources.temporal_coverage: Open-access chapter published 2025; reviews climate-adaptation governance and source-reported conflict examples, including a 2004 drought case.
sources.methodology: Qualitative text analysis of policies, government data, public records and climate/conflict literature.
sources.limitations: Document review, not primary causal research; authors say Thailand linkages remain understudied.

sources.title: Gender Equality and Social Inclusion Analysis (Thailand, 2025)
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 gender and social inclusion study prepared for the CINTALAM youth-led climate-action project.
sources.methodology: Publisher abstract describes the study as mixed-methods; extracted findings are limited to that official abstract.
sources.limitations: Full report PDF was not retrievable; sample, detailed methods and locality-level results were not inspected, and the abstract does not establish causal effects.

sources.title: Women leading peace and climate resilience in southern Thailand
sources.organization: United Nations in Thailand / UN Women
sources.temporal_coverage: UN story published 2 April 2026; includes participant accounts and captions on the Yupo flood of 25 November 2025.
sources.methodology: Qualitative UN country feature profiles women and community organizations, with named-site observations, participant accounts and captions.
sources.limitations: A feature story, not representative monitoring or climate-attribution research; local event estimates and reported experiences are not population-level measures.

claims.locator: Chapter 3, printed p. 32, Table 3-1, water-resources risk areas
claims.paraphrase: Bangkok, Nakhon Ratchasima and Ubon Ratchathani recur among the top-ten modeled heat, drought and flood risk areas for water management under both RCP lists.
institutions: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment
claims.limitations: These are province-level model rankings reproduced from ONEP 2021, not observed impacts; the 2016–2035 projection period is partly elapsed.

claims.locator: Chapter 3, printed p. 37, Table 3-2, agriculture and food-security risk areas
claims.paraphrase: For agriculture, Nakhon Ratchasima, Khon Kaen and Ubon Ratchathani appear in both modeled RCP top-ten lists for drought risk.
claims.limitations: Model ranks identify relative provincial risk, not measured crop losses or household-level effects; the underlying assessment is attributed to ONEP 2021.

claims.locator: Chapter 3, printed p. 61, Table 3-6, human settlements and security sector
claims.paraphrase: Bangkok and Nakhon Ratchasima occur in both modeled flood-risk top-ten lists for the NAP's human-settlements-and-security sector.
claims.limitations: The plan's security-sector label is a planning category, not a finding about violent conflict; rankings are dated model outputs, not observed events.

claims.locator: Chapter 1, printed p. 1, paragraph beginning 'Incomes and wealth are concentrated in Bangkok'
claims.paraphrase: The CCDR contrasts Bangkok's high urban-flood exposure with drought, water shortages and rainfall variability affecting poorer Northern and Northeastern provinces and agriculture.
claims.limitations: Regional diagnosis rather than household-level estimation; the paragraph does not attribute all current water shortages to anthropogenic climate change.

claims.locator: Annex 2, opening paragraph, 'Resolving dual water challenges in Khon Kaen Province'
claims.paraphrase: The report describes recurring drought and floods in Khon Kaen; 2021 floods averaged three months, while water insecurity deepened poverty among low-income agriculturists.
claims.limitations: The annex describes provincial conditions and an observed 2021 flood period; it does not estimate climate-attributable poverty or household prevalence.

claims.locator: Annex 2, subsection 'Khon Kaen's Attempt' and following 'Implications and Lessons'
claims.paraphrase: Khon Kaen's water subcommittee convened 14 agencies and local stakeholders; risk mapping and consultation informed an integrated plan and a five-municipality urban-flood project.
claims.limitations: The report documents planning and a signed municipal agreement, not resilience outcomes; it notes centralized mandates, limited budget autonomy and weak local-government capacity constrain replication.

claims.paraphrase: In the chapter's cited Songkhla 2004 case, drought-related expected rice losses preceded farmer stockpiling, BRN-C raids on fields and a reported 90% rise in insurgent killings.
claims.limitations: Secondary-cited temporal account, not independent causality; 90% is reported for the drought period only.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Authors link drought-related rice scarcity to BRN-C raids and increased insurgent killings.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: Section 3.3, paragraph beginning 'Adverse climatic conditions can also result in violent conflicts'.

claims.locator: Section 3.3, discussion of resource-based conflicts and climate-related scarcity
claims.paraphrase: Authors say climate-related scarcity and weather-driven migration can intensify conflict; Thai upstream-downstream water disputes commonly accompany floods and droughts.
claims.scenario: Conditional future pathway; no quantitative scenario or date stated.
claims.limitations: Conceptual synthesis; political history is a stronger predictor and Thailand-specific evidence is understudied.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Authors link scarcity/migration to conflict and report water disputes during flood/drought periods.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: Section 3.3, paragraphs on resource scarcity, migration and Thai upstream-downstream water conflict.

claims.locator: Section 3.2, civil-society discussion on climate justice and local capacity-building
claims.paraphrase: The chapter notes Thai NGOs and researchers provide participatory adaptation research and capacity-building for vulnerable communities.
institutions: Thai Working Group for Climate Justice

claims.locator: Save the Children Resource Centre page, official abstract, opening summary
claims.paraphrase: The study abstract describes climate change, conflict and gender inequality as mutually reinforcing pressures harming marginalized communities in the Southern Border Provinces.
claims.limitations: This is the publisher's abstract-level characterization; the report's full text and its specific causal mechanisms were not inspected.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The abstract explicitly characterizes climate change, conflict and gender inequality as mutually reinforcing pressures on marginalized communities.

claims.locator: Save the Children Resource Centre page, official abstract, findings paragraph
claims.paraphrase: The abstract says widows and single mothers face combined unpaid household work, income-generation and crisis-volunteering burdens, with higher debt, unequal land ownership and gender stereotypes.
claims.limitations: Abstract summary gives no sample size or disaggregated provincial estimates; it does not attribute every burden specifically to climate shocks.

claims.locator: Save the Children Resource Centre page, official abstract, structural-gaps and recommendations paragraphs
claims.paraphrase: The abstract identifies weak gender integration in local climate policies and missing gender-disaggregated data; it recommends stronger local-institution capacity and inclusive climate solutions.
claims.limitations: Recommendations are not evidence of implementation; only the resource-page abstract was inspected, not the full report.

claims.locator: Yupo community profile, paragraphs on changing weather and rubber/small-scale farming
claims.paraphrase: In Yupo Subdistrict, Yala, women describe irregular rain, long droughts and severe floods disrupting rubber-tapping and small-farm livelihoods and raising crop-pumping fuel costs.
institutions: UN Women Women’s Empowerment and Learning Centre Yupo
claims.limitations: Participant accounts in a local feature story; it gives no measured rainfall series or formal climate-attribution analysis.

claims.locator: Yupo flood caption and profile, 25 November 2025 event
claims.paraphrase: The story caption reports floodwaters over 2.5 metres in Yupo on 25 November 2025, leaving approximately 300 families stranded.
institutions: UN Women Women’s Empowerment and Learning Centre Yupo
claims.limitations: The figure is a story caption estimate, not a systematic needs assessment or a complete count of affected people.

claims.locator: Yupo flood-preparedness profile and Masjid Raudatul Jannah caption
claims.paraphrase: Yupo networks share early warnings, food and supplies; during the November 2025 flood, a mosque sheltered 50 residents and a community kitchen served about 300 families.
institutions: UN Women Women’s Empowerment and Learning Centre Yupo
claims.limitations: The article reports one community's practices and one flood event; it does not measure response coverage or effects on conflict dynamics.

search_audit.query: Thailand province climate vulnerability RCP heat drought flood National Adaptation Plan Bangkok Khon Kaen 2016 2035
search_audit.outcome: Read the NAP provincial risk tables, World Bank Bangkok/North/Northeast diagnosis and Khon Kaen case, plus the named Yupo local profile; model vintages and local anecdotal scope are stated in claims.

search_audit.query: Thailand climate conflict drought water scarcity migration Songkhla 2004 BRN adaptation conflict primary report
search_audit.outcome: The open Springer chapter reports a secondary-cited 2004 Songkhla drought/BRN-C rice-field-raid case and broader conditional scarcity/migration pathways; it stresses political history as stronger predictor and says Thailand links remain understudied. Save the Children abstract separately describes mutually reinforcing climate, conflict and gender pressures. A 2026 publisher article was inaccessible and its indexed text was excluded.

search_audit.query: Thailand conflict insecurity limits adaptation climate services climate adaptation access southern border provinces report
search_audit.outcome: No inspected primary source established that conflict or insecurity prevented climate-adaptation implementation or service access. The Springer review and UN Women story describe conflict-affected settings but do not document that reverse pathway; this remains an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.

search_audit.query: Thailand local adaptation capacity community early warning social protection integrated Khon Kaen water plan local institutions
search_audit.outcome: Read the Khon Kaen integrated-planning case, the NAP risk-monitoring framework, World Bank recommendations and Yupo's local warning/shelter practices. These document processes or recommendations, not evaluated peace or resilience outcomes.

gaps: No existing THA country baseline was present in EXISTING_COUNTRIES.json.
Thailand's 2026 Taylor & Francis climate-conflict article was not used: direct publisher access returned 403, so indexed text remains leads-only.
The Fourth National Communication timed out and the Fourth Biennial Update Report exceeded retrieval limits; no claims rely on their indexed excerpts.
The Save the Children PDF was inaccessible; its findings are limited to the official resource-page abstract, which does not provide sample details or province-level results.
The 2004 Songkhla drought-conflict pathway is a secondary-cited historical account in a 2025 document-analysis chapter, not independent causal identification.
No inspected primary source documented conflict or insecurity directly blocking climate-adaptation implementation or services; this remains a search gap.
